newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to set 1997 Eurobond volumes after April.
newsitem.headline: Russia to set 1997 Eurobond volumes after April.

text.p: The exact volume of Eurobonds to be issued this year by the Russian government will be decided no earlier than the end of April, Finance Minister Alexander Livshits said.
"We will know the value and the currency of the issue more exactly only at the end of April," Livshits told Reuters.
He said that the Ministry of Finance has a schedule "in terms of months, amounts, and currencies" for issuing the bonds on world markets, but he declined to give further details.

Deputy Finance Minister Mikhail Kasyanov said earlier this month that Russia planned to issue several Eurobonds in a number of different currencies with a total value of $3 billion by the end of the year.
Livshits said the market will determine the exact volume of the second Eurobond issue, to be issued in marks. Kasyanov said this issue, planned for March, would be about one billion marks.
The Finance Ministry is currently drawing up selection criteria for co-managers of the second Russian Eurobond.
"The co-managers for the most part will be large German banks," said Livshits. "However, there will also be some Russian banks."
Russia has already appointed Deutsche Morgan Grenfell and CS First Boston as lead managers of the issue.
Russia issued its debut Eurobond, a highly oversubscribed $1 billion issue, in November 1996.
